eras.name: Classic RL
eras.background: Dynamic programming solved decision problems when the environment's model was known. Temporal-difference learning and Q-learning learned from experience instead, and policy gradients optimized policies directly, but only small problems fit in tables.

eras.name: Deep RL
eras.text: Neural networks as value and policy
eras.background: Neural networks let agents learn from raw pixels and act in continuous spaces once training was stabilized. Combined with tree search and self-play, they beat the best human Go players.

eras.name: Learning from feedback
eras.text: Rewards from people and checked answers
eras.background: Many real goals have no written reward. Rewards learned from human comparisons, and later from automatically checked answers, made RL the final stage of training language models.

nodes.label: Dynamic programming
nodes.problem: The effects of a decision play out over many later steps.
nodes.idea: Bellman's equation defines a state's value recursively, solvable when the model is known.
nodes.impact: The foundation that every RL method approximates.

nodes.label: TD learning
nodes.idea: Update predictions from the difference between successive estimates.
nodes.impact: The core update of value-based RL; TD-Gammon used it to play backgammon near expert level.

from.why: Dynamic programming needs a model of the environment, and waiting for final outcomes is slow.

nodes.label: Q-learning
nodes.idea: Learn action values that converge to optimal under any exploring policy.
nodes.impact: The base algorithm that DQN later scaled up.

from.why: TD learned how good states are, but choosing actions needs action values learned while exploring.

nodes.label: REINFORCE
nodes.problem: Neural policies needed a way to follow the reward gradient without a model.
nodes.idea: Estimate the gradient of expected reward from sampled actions and the returns they earned.
nodes.impact: The ancestor of policy-gradient methods, PPO included.

nodes.label: DQN
nodes.idea: Experience replay and a target network stabilize learning from pixels.
nodes.impact: One network learned many Atari games, starting deep RL.

from.why: Q-learning worked on small tables but diverged when paired with neural networks.

nodes.label: AlphaGo
nodes.idea: Guide tree search with policy and value networks trained on human games and self-play.
nodes.impact: Beat Lee Sedol, years before experts expected a machine to.

from.why: Exhaustive search is impossible in Go's enormous game tree.

nodes.label: PPO
nodes.idea: Clip the update so each step stays close to the old policy.
nodes.impact: The default policy-gradient algorithm, and the RL step of RLHF.

from.why: Plain policy gradients are noisy, and a large step can collapse the policy; TRPO's fix was complex.

nodes.label: MuZero
nodes.idea: Learn a model that predicts only reward, policy and value, and plan with it.
nodes.impact: Matched AlphaZero at board games and extended planning to Atari.

from.why: Its search needed the game's rules to simulate moves.

nodes.label: Human preferences
nodes.problem: Many goals cannot be written down as a reward function.
nodes.idea: Fit a reward model to people's comparisons of behavior, then optimize against it.
nodes.impact: The method later used to align language models.

nodes.label: RLHF
nodes.idea: Optimize the language model with PPO against a reward model of human preferences.
nodes.impact: Turned GPT-3 into InstructGPT and ChatGPT.

from.why: Supplied a way to turn human comparisons into a reward.
Supplied a stable algorithm for optimizing a large model against that reward.

nodes.label: Reasoning RL
nodes.idea: Reward answers that can be verified automatically, such as math and code.
nodes.impact: Taught models such as DeepSeek-R1 to reason at length.

from.why: Preference labels are costly and cannot check whether a hard answer is right.

main.title: Stanford CS234: Reinforcement Learning
main.why: MDPs, TD and Q-learning up to DQN, policy gradients up to PPO, imitation, RLHF and DPO, offline RL, bandits and tree search. In English.

main.title: Learning to Predict by the Methods of Temporal Differences
main.why: Waiting for final outcomes makes learning slow, so temporal-difference methods learn from the difference between successive predictions.

further.why: To find more efficient matches, Lyft estimates each driver's future earnings in real time with online RL and matches on them.

main.title: Human-Level Control through Deep Reinforcement Learning
main.why: Q-learning with neural networks was unstable, so DQN adds experience replay and a target network to learn Atari games from pixels.

further.title: Rainbow: Combining Improvements in Deep Reinforcement Learning

main.title: Simple Statistical Gradient-Following Algorithms for Connectionist Reinforcement Learning
main.why: Without a model of the environment, REINFORCE follows the gradient of expected reward estimated from sampled actions and rewards.

main.title: Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms
main.why: TRPO is complex to implement, so PPO clips its objective to get similarly safe steps from plain minibatch updates.

further.title: Implementation Matters in Deep Policy Gradients: A Case Study on PPO and TRPO
Trust Region Policy Optimization
further.why: Large policy-gradient steps can collapse a policy, so TRPO keeps each update inside a KL-divergence trust region.

main.title: Soft Actor-Critic: Off-Policy Maximum Entropy Deep Reinforcement Learning with a Stochastic Actor
main.why: Deep RL for continuous control was sample-hungry and brittle, so SAC learns off-policy while maximizing reward plus entropy.

main.title: Mastering the Game of Go without Human Knowledge
main.why: AlphaGo Zero drops human games and learns from self-play alone, with tree search as the teacher for its network.

further.title: Mastering the Game of Go with Deep Neural Networks and Tree Search
further.why: Go is too large for brute-force search, so AlphaGo guides tree search with policy and value networks trained on human games and self-play.

main.title: Mastering Atari, Go, Chess and Shogi by Planning with a Learned Model
main.why: Planning usually needs the game's rules, so MuZero plans with a learned model that predicts only reward, policy and value.

main.title: Mastering Diverse Control Tasks through World Models
main.why: RL algorithms usually need retuning for each domain, so DreamerV3 learns a world model and trains in imagined rollouts with one fixed configuration.

main.title: A Reduction of Imitation Learning and Structured Prediction to No-Regret Online Learning
main.why: A cloned policy drifts into states the expert never showed, so DAgger has the expert label the states the learner visits.

main.title: Conservative Q-Learning for Offline Reinforcement Learning
main.why: Offline RL overestimates actions missing from the data, so CQL pushes their Q-values down while training on a fixed dataset.

background.title: Offline Reinforcement Learning: Tutorial, Review, and Perspectives on Open Problems

main.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning from Human Preferences
main.why: Many tasks lack a reward function, so a reward model fit to human comparisons of short clips trains the agent instead.

main.title: A Contextual-Bandit Approach to Personalized News Article Recommendation
main.why: New articles need exploration, so LinUCB picks Yahoo front-page news by upper confidence bounds over user and article features.

background.title: Finite-Time Analysis of the Multiarmed Bandit Problem

further.title: An Empirical Evaluation of Thompson Sampling

further.why: Heuristics decided which map area to search, so Airbnb frames it as a contextual bandit that explores with UCB on dropout-based uncertainty.

main.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning at the Edge of the Statistical Precipice
main.why: Point estimates from a few runs per task mislead, so report bootstrap intervals, performance profiles and interquartile means.

main.title: Top-K Off-Policy Correction for a REINFORCE Recommender System
main.why: Logs from older recommenders bias policy learning, so YouTube trains a REINFORCE recommender with off-policy correction.
